Compile a model into an execution plan

Source: R/compile.R
sim_compile.Rd

Compilation turns a mutable sim_model() into an immutable sim_plan in these stages:

Usage

sim_compile(
  model,
  algebraic_loops = c("error", "solve"),
  loop_tol = 1e-10,
  loop_maxit = 50,
  loop_guess = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A sim_model().

algebraic_loops

"error" (default) or "solve".

loop_tol

Absolute residual tolerance for loop solving.

loop_maxit

Maximum Newton iterations per loop solve.

loop_guess

Optional named list of starting values for loop solving, keyed by signal name (as in sim_signal()); each value has the length of that signal.

Value

A sim_plan object. Use sim_run() to simulate it, sim_set_params() to change parameters and sim_diagnostics() to inspect the analysis.

Details

  1. Flatten subsystems and resolve sim_param() references.

  2. Build every block and validate its parameters.

  3. Validate connections: blocks and ports exist and every input has exactly one source.

  4. Propagate signal sizes along connections and check compatibility.

  5. Build the direct-feedthrough dependency graph. There is an edge from block A to block B when an output of A feeds an input of B that has direct feedthrough. Inputs of integrators, unit delays and other state-output blocks create no edge, so feedback through them is valid.

  6. Find strongly connected components of that graph. A component with more than one block, or a block feeding itself, is an algebraic loop.

  7. Order the blocks topologically. Ties are broken by block name, so the order, the state vector layout and the results do not depend on the order in which blocks or connections were added.

  8. Lay out the signal, continuous state and discrete state vectors and collect sample times, zero-crossing functions and events.

Algebraic loops are rejected by default. With algebraic_loops = "solve" each loop is solved at every evaluation by Newton iterations on the loop outputs, with a finite-difference Jacobian and backtracking; the run fails with an error when the residual does not fall below loop_tol. Every solve starts from loop_guess where given and from zero otherwise, so results never depend on the history of solver trial points. A loop with several solutions (for example y = 4 / y) is steered to one of them by its starting value.

Examples

m <- sim_model("feedback")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "r", value = 1)
sim_add_block(m, "subtract", "e")
sim_add_block(m, "integrator", "x")
sim_connect(m, "r", "e", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "x", "e", input = 2)
sim_connect(m, "e", "x")
plan <- sim_compile(m)
plan
#> <sim_plan 'feedback'> 3 block(s), 1 continuous state(s), 0 discrete state(s), 3 signal element(s)
#> Execution order: r > x > e
sim_diagnostics(plan)$order
#> [1] "r" "x" "e"

# A loop of direct-feedthrough blocks is an algebraic loop.
m2 <- sim_model("loop")
sim_add_block(m2, "constant", "u", value = 1)
sim_add_block(m2, "sum", "s", signs = "+-")
sim_add_block(m2, "gain", "k", gain = 2)
sim_connect(m2, "u", "s", input = 1)
sim_connect(m2, "k", "s", input = 2)
sim_connect(m2, "s", "k")
try(sim_compile(m2))
#> Error : Algebraic loop(s) detected: every block on the cycle has direct feedthrough, so the outputs depend on themselves at the same time.
#>   k -> s -> k
#> Break the loop with a stateful block (integrator, unit_delay, ...) or compile with algebraic_loops = "solve".
plan2 <- sim_compile(m2, algebraic_loops = "solve")
sim_signal(sim_run(plan2, c(0, 1), times = 1), "s") # y = 1 - 2y, so 1/3
#>         s 
#> 0.3333333
